brief: Today's posts were dominated by reports and reactions about Nvidia's board and Jensen Huang, with commentators questioning the timing and calling for due process. Beyond that, builders discussed AI-native infrastructure, with Nikunj Kothari's sub-processor scrape showing more companies using two or more model providers.

themes.label: Nvidia board and Jensen Huang
themes.summary: Builders reacted to reports about Nvidia's board ousting Jensen Huang, questioning the timing, defending his leadership, and calling for a proper investigation.

themes.label: Google Labs Tabletop
themes.summary: Google Labs introduced Tabletop, a shared-space experiment that generates custom interactive spaces on the fly, and showed how its team uses it at home.

themes.label: AI-native company infrastructure
themes.summary: Nikunj Kothari's scrape of 803 companies' sub-processor lists found more firms using multiple model providers and inference providers than in March.

builders.name: AI & I by Every
builders.summary: Podcast episode on human work after automation, recapping Every's first conference in Brooklyn and Dan Shipper's closing talk.

builders.name: Thariq
builders.summary: Said the experience of using coding agents could look different next year, and promoted his AIE talk titled "the sweet side of the bitter lesson".

builders.name: Nikunj Kothari
builders.summary: Shared findings from scraping 803 AI-native companies' sub-processors, noting more multi-provider use and Anthropic's faster growth. Also posted a request for startups and minor replies.

builders.name: Claude
builders.summary: Highlighted artist Mariko Mori using Claude to write code for a computer-generated animation in her retrospective "All That Shines."

builders.name: Aditya Agarwal
builders.summary: Framed two kinds of companies to build: diffusing AI into existing work and pursuing the frontier of scientific progress, citing examples at SPC. Also praised partner Rox.

builders.name: Dan Shipper
builders.summary: Wrote that a single person with AI now does work that once took a team, citing his week building a CRM and game and citing GDPval results rising to about 83%.

builders.name: Guillermo Rauch
builders.summary: Posted about a benchmark comparing fx bootup to an assembly version, promoted Beam by Reflection as free until Nov 12, and wrote that great products need sustained human effort.

builders.name: Matt Turck
builders.summary: Posted brief reactions, including a note that the post had gems for founders and a comment on French execs in the Jensen story.

builders.name: Amjad Masad
builders.summary: Questioned why old stories about Jensen Huang suddenly became international news, asking who benefits and pointing to the midterms and upcoming IPOs.

builders.name: Google Labs
builders.summary: Announced Tabletop, an experiment for turning shared links and files into custom spaces, and shared a family-use tour of it.

builders.name: Swyx
builders.summary: Posted about keynote attendance, a stream with typesafeai, and a clarification about a former employee. Mostly brief event and community updates.

builders.name: Garry Tan
builders.summary: Argued Nvidia's board was ill advised to oust Jensen Huang. Otherwise posted event registration notices for an Acts 17 event with Huberman Lab.

builders.name: Peter Steinberger
builders.summary: Briefly said that open source is hard enough without politics, responding to comments.

builders.name: Josh Woodward
builders.summary: Said the team builds regularly with a product that makes their apps faster and smarter.

builders.name: Peter Yang
builders.summary: Voiced disappointment in Jensen Huang and later argued the board should investigate and involve shareholders before acting.

builders.name: Thibault Sottiaux
builders.summary: Posted two short personal remarks about Codex and a banked reset, with no technical detail.

builders.name: Zara Zhang
builders.summary: Shared a quote that technology finishes its most important work once the audience forgets it. Otherwise personal or minor.
